author: Codex root
scope: critical acceptance review; no source changes

sources.verified: NEXT_ID is a read trigger; controlled HOLD locks base writes; COUNT is first public backend VALID and freezes ownership under the launch contract; WAIT waits actual parent COPY completion. Pool allocation/chosen slot return do not currently exist.

Single query port; context/stage/page-size matching; content contains permission fields, but tag hit alone is not an access decision. No-touch is supported when TouchEnable=true and touch_i=false. Replacement/invalidations remain independent.

Actual instantiation sets TouchEnable(NonblockEnable); root observed normal wrapper permission checks using content W/R/X/U on hits. Therefore do not treat the IOTLB module default parameter as proof production always changes PLRU on hints.
PROC_PTE can set state_n=MEM_ACCESS and next pointer; no inherent long fixed gap between successful PTE return and next request.

worker_corrections.correction: Chosen destination must be stable BEFORE first VALID, not merely before first READY/handshake.
next_id.re is a read event, not a write of NEXT_ID.
HOLD using live config is not by itself evidence of a reachable mutation bug because controlled launch rejects writes. New proposed path still needs frozen parameters or equivalent locking.
Frontend burst_req_t is a parent COPY descriptor. Completion after the first normal DEFAULT request is not proof only one AXI data burst is copied.
No independent allow/deny output is correct; claiming content lacks permission bits is too broad. The wrapper consumes content_1S.w/r/x/u and stage2 fields.
Use actual TouchEnable(NonblockEnable), not module default, for active implementation. No-touch support does not create a free concurrent lookup port.
